subject: Drawdown staircase proposal for 3-year committed usage
messages:

Subject: Committed spend structure — ask for drawdown options

Olga / Aditya,

Thanks for the materials on pricing earlier. Our finance team asked us to propose two options for a 3-year committed spend: one with a smooth annual prepay and one with a multi-year drawdown (a staircase) tied to usage ramp expectations.

Specifically, they want to understand:
- How a staircase drawdown would be billed (monthly amortization vs wallet burn).
- Treatment of unused prepay at year-ends and at contract termination.
- If discounts vary by year / ramp (we expect Year 1 lower commit, Year 3 higher).
- Any accounting-friendly amortization schedule you can provide for CapEx approvals.

Could you send a short proposal and a sample drawdown schedule we can share with procurement and legal? We plan to make a recommendation to procurement by Nov 5.

Thanks,
Lara Dean
Head of Cloud Procurement, Nexera Cloud

Subject: Re: Committed spend structure — ask for drawdown options

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear asks. Attached: a draft SOW (Nexera_Draft_SOW_v3.pdf) and a sample drawdown_schedule.xlsx that outlines two candidate structures. Summary below.

Option A — Annual Prepay (simple)
- 3-year term; customer prepays Year 1/Year 2/Year 3 amounts at start of each year.
- Discount tiers tied to annual committed $ (Year 1: 12%, Year 2: 15%, Year 3: 18%).
- Unused prepay at year-end rolls into a 30-day true-up window; after 30 days remaining credit converts to refundable balance (subject to minimum fees).

Option B — Drawdown Staircase (recommended for ramping growth)
- Customer prepays a multi-year wallet at signature (e.g., 60% Year 1, 80% Year 2, 100% Year 3 nominal capacity) or funds can be staged with scheduled tranche payments.
- Billing model: live usage consumes the wallet first (burn model). Monthly invoices show amortized SEV (service entitlement value) and net wallet burn.
- Discounts: larger effective discount if customer commits to multi-year wallet upfront (examples in sheet: upfront 3-year prepay = additional 4% across the term).
- True-ups: quarterly usage true-up with a 45-day reconciliation window; unspent wallet funds at contract termination are refunded per SOW schedule (standard amortization over remaining term or refundable minus early-termination fee).

Operational notes:
- We support month-by-month burn reporting in Console and an accounting CSV export for CapEx/Amortization.
- For enterprise accounting we can provide an amortization table (attached in Excel) that maps prepaid amounts to monthly P&L recognition.

Next steps: if you prefer Option B, we can produce an amortization schedule that maps to Nexera's fiscal quarters and produce a DocuSign-ready amendment with tranche payment dates.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nexera_Draft_SOW_v3.pdf, drawdown_schedule.xlsx

Lara — quick operational clarifications from the infra/ops side: please see inline.

On Option B (wallet burn):
- Wallet consumption is first-in-first-out per request until wallet exhausted; we support live routing to fallback models if wallet balance is low (this is configurable per route).
- Monthly invoices will show tokens consumed and wallet balance; we can also provide per-model cost breakdown.
- Throttling: if consumption exceeds committed throughput policies, we can apply soft-throttles or fallback to on-demand pricing for overflow. If you want a hard cap, we should note that in the SOW.

Accounting/export: The Console CSV includes per-month recognized spend and a prepaid_balance line; we can add an amortization column for Nexera's finance team.

If Nexera wants staged tranches instead of a single upfront wallet, we'll need the tranche dates to configure capacity reservations.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference

Hi Lara — quick answers to procurement/legal asks below and references to where we updated the SOW (attached).

1) Early-termination refund example (illustrative):
- Customer prepays $3,000,000 for a 3-year wallet. After 18 months, consumed = $1,080,000. Remaining prepaid = $1,920,000. Refund calculation per SOW: refundable_balance = remaining_prepaid - (early_termination_fee of 5% of remaining_prepaid) = $1,824,000.
- All amortization tables are provided in the Excel; we can also produce CSV keyed to Nexera GL codes if required.

2) 12-month true-up: yes — we can offer an annual true-up instead of quarterly for deals >= $2.5M/yr committed. We'll note this as an option and add a clause: "Annual true-up window: 60 days after fiscal year close; adjustments applied to next invoice or refunded per termination rules."

3) Overflow/on-demand cap: yes — we can contractually cap on-demand pricing for overflow to a fixed per-token multiple (example: 1.6x the committed blended rate) for planning purposes. Exact cap to be listed in the SOW under Section 4.2.

We updated the SOW to include: termination example, annual true-up option, and capped overflow language. Attached: Nexera_Draft_SOW_v3.pdf (redlines) and updated drawdown_schedule.xlsx.

If Nexera confirms Option B with annual true-up, we'll prepare a DocuSign amendment with tranche schedule and an amortization CSV that maps to Nexera fiscal months.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
